{{Short description|German physicist}}
'''Beate Naroska''' (1943 – 17 February 2008) was a [[Germany|German]] physicist and professor at the [[University of Hamburg]] who worked in the field of [[particle physics]].<ref>{{cite journal |title=Beate Naroska 1943–2008 |journal=CERN Courier |date=June 2008 |volume=48 |issue=5 |url=https://repository.cern/records/t9sqx-pm927?preview_file=vol48-issue5.pdf |publisher=Plein and Baus GmnH |location=Burscheid |language=en}}</ref>

== Career ==
From 1972 until 1978, Naroska worked at [[CERN]], working with a group led by [[Carlo Rubbia]] on diffractive processes.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=XXVIII PHYSICS IN COLLISION |url=https://agenda.infn.it/event/141/contributions/22973/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250717223535/https://agenda.infn.it/event/141/contributions/22973/ |archive-date=2025-07-17 |access-date=2025-11-21 |website=Agenda (Indico) |language=en}}</ref> In 1978, Naroska returned to [[DESY]], where she worked on the [[JADE (particle detector)|JADE]] collaboration, working with particle accelerators.<ref name=":1" /> 

In 1989, Naroska became a professor at the University of Hamburg.<ref name=":1" /> From 1989 until 2005, Naroska was a part of the University of Hamburg's Department of Physics until 2005, and then served the rest of her years on the departments of mathematics, computer science, and natural sciences until her death on February 17, 2008.<ref name=":2">https://www.hpk.uni-hamburg.de/resolve/id/cph_person_00003185 The official website of the University of Hamburg. This contains dates of her time in different departments at the university. </ref>
